title: How much cash did Apple’s business generate?
introduction: Start with Net Income, then follow Apple’s reported operating-cash reconciliation.
boundary: Operating Cash Flow is cash generated by operating activities during the year. It is not Apple’s year-end cash balance.

depreciation-and-amortization.helper: A non-cash adjustment in Apple’s operating reconciliation.

share-based-compensation-expense.helper: Another non-cash adjustment reported by Apple.

accounts-receivable-net.helper: An operating timing adjustment related to customer amounts owed.

vendor-non-trade-receivables.helper: An operating timing adjustment related to supplier amounts owed to Apple.

inventories.helper: The operating-cash effect of Apple’s inventory change.

other-current-and-non-current-assets.helper: The reported operating-cash effect of changes in other assets.

accounts-payable.helper: The operating-cash effect of changes in amounts Apple owed suppliers.

other-current-and-non-current-liabilitie.helper: The reported operating-cash effect of changes in other liabilities.

cash-generated-by-operating-activities.helper: Apple’s reported total for operating activities during FY2025.

firstQuestion.prompt: Did Apple generate exactly the same amount of operating cash as Net Income?
firstQuestion.hint: Choose one. This is practice, not a score.

choices.label: Yes — Net Income is the cash Apple generated.
Not necessarily — profit and operating cash are different measures.

firstQuestion.supportedFeedback: Net Income is an accounting result. Cash generated by operations is a different measure.
firstQuestion.unsupportedFeedback: Net Income measures accounting profit. It does not tell us exactly how much operating cash the business generated.

finalQuestion.prompt: What does Apple’s Operating Cash Flow figure tell you?
finalQuestion.hint: Choose one. This is practice, not a score.

choices.label: It is Apple’s Net Income for FY2025.
It is the cash Apple held at year end.
It is cash Apple generated from operating activities during FY2025.

finalQuestion.supportedFeedback: This is cash generated by Apple’s operating activities during the period. It is different from Net Income and from the cash balance at year end.
finalQuestion.netIncomeFeedback: Net Income is a different reported figure. It is the accounting-profit starting point in this reconciliation.
finalQuestion.cashBalanceFeedback: Operating Cash Flow is a flow during the year, not the amount of cash Apple held at year end.

limitation: Operating Cash Flow alone does not tell you how much Apple invested in long-term assets, how it financed the business, how much cash it held at year end, whether its shares are fairly priced, or whether Apple is a good investment.

verification.unitNote: Apple reports this statement in USD millions. FinPath displays large figures in USD billions.
verification.displayNote: Signed adjustments follow Apple’s cash-flow presentation. Parentheses indicate a negative effect in the reconciliation.

sources.title: Apple FY2025 Form 10-K — Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
